title: The Calvin cycle: counting the carbon
caption: Three turns fix three CO₂ (1 carbon each) onto three RuBP (5 carbons each), giving six GP (3 carbons each). The GP is reduced to six triose phosphate; five of them regenerate three RuBP and one leaves to make sugars. Carbon is conserved at every step: 18 in, 18 out, and one triose phosphate gained from three CO₂.
alt: A cycle of RuBP, GP and triose phosphate: RuBisCO fixes CO2 onto RuBP to give GP, GP is reduced to triose phosphate, and triose phosphate regenerates RuBP, with one triose phosphate in six leaving.
description: Fixation: 3 CO₂ + 3 RuBP (5C) become 6 GP (3C): 18 carbons in, 18 out.
Reduction: 6 GP become 6 triose phosphate using ATP and NADPH: 18 carbons.
Regeneration: 5 triose phosphate (15C) are rearranged into 3 RuBP (15C) using ATP.
One triose phosphate (3C) leaves for each three CO₂ fixed; six turns make one glucose (6C).
notes: One triose phosphate in six leaves the cycle to make sugars; six turns fix six CO₂ into one glucose.
